lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: MT-135 implemented. MECHANISM (AC-135-2, generalises without an allowlist): egui 0.33.3 keeps AT MOST ONE open popup per viewport - a single OpenPopup{id,pos} slot in egui::Memory. Top menu-bar dropdowns, pane/tab/tree/editor context menus and any future Popup::menu / Popup::context_menu / Popup::open_memory caller all funnel through that one slot, so copying it projects EVERY memory-backed popup surface, present and future, with no registration step for a new menu. egui exposes no public 'which popup is open' getter (Memory::popups is private), so the new module accessibility/popup_projection.rs composes two public halves: Memory::areas().visible_layer_ids() (an open popup always has a visible layer, because Popup::show renders through Area::new(popup_id)) probed by Popup::is_id_open for exact match. Only one can match, so the unordered HashSet cannot make it nondeterministic. The stored POSITION is load-bearing, not polish: Popup::context_menu uses PopupAnchor::PointerFixed, so re-opening without the position yields anchor.rect == None and egui SILENTLY RENDERS NOTHING - a position-less projection would have looked like a fix while publishing nothing. WHY THE MT-121 COORDINATE CONTRACT SURVIVES (AC-135-3): only egui::Id + Option<Pos2> crosses the context boundary. No focus, no Memory::data (where scroll offsets and widget state live), no area geometry, no interaction state. The blanket Memory clone that the contract's red-team flagged is explicitly rejected in the module docs. Proven rather than asserted: published and rendered bounds for the menu leaf matched with ZERO delta - published=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) rendered=(x=381.000, y=286.000, w=586.000, h=18.000) - and the whole-tree viewport guard was re-run WITH a menu projected. The MT-121 theme-toggle proof is unchanged and still exact. PT-135-1 RED (verbatim): 3 tests failed, including the inverted witness - "AC-135-1: 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' is open in the live rendered frame, so it MUST appear in the published MCP snapshot". PT-135-1 GREEN (verbatim): 'test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed'. PT-135-3 CLOSED-MENU PROOF (AC-135-5) checks two closed states that fail differently: never-opened (a projection that force-opened menus would publish it) and opened-then-dismissed-with-Escape (a latching or stale projection would keep publishing a menu the operator dismissed). Runtime line: never_opened=false while_open=true after_escape=false. Stale entries cannot leak because Memory::end_pass drops any popup not kept open during the pass and the projection is read fresh per capture, never cached. scope.summary: HandshakeApp::refresh_mcp_snapshot builds a BRAND-NEW egui::Context for the model-vision capture pass. That fresh context has an EMPTY egui::Memory, so any surface whose open/closed state lives in egui::Memory is absent from the published MCP snapshot even when it is visibly open in the live window. app.rs already works around this for two surfaces by hand-copying the Reading-mode store and the open top-menu into the capture context, but pointer-opened PANE CONTEXT MENUS have no such projection. Consequence: a model driving Argus cannot see, target, or steer any context menu - it is invisible in argus.inspect while a human sees it on screen. This was proven live during MT-121 by tests/test_mcp_snapshot_viewport.rs::mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass, which shows author_id 'ctx-menu.pane.pop_out' present in the rendered kittest frame and absent from the published snapshot. MT-121 fixed viewport SIZING only and deliberately did not fix this; the failing condition is asserted as current behaviour there, so that assertion MUST be inverted by this MT.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pane context menu that is open in the live window appears in the published MCP snapshot with its stable author_id, role and bounds, exactly as it appears in the rendered AccessKit tree.

The projection is general, not a hard-coded allowlist of one menu: any egui::Memory-backed surface the shell can open is projected into the capture context by a single documented mechanism, and adding a new menu does not require a new bespoke copy step.
Bounds published for the projected menu lie inside the declared SnapshotViewport and match the rendered frame, preserving the MT-121 coordinate contract.

The MT-121 test mt121_memory_backed_context_menu_remains_invisible_to_the_sized_capture_pass is inverted to assert the menu IS visible, and its comment is updated so it no longer documents the defect as expected behaviour.
A closed context menu is still absent from the snapshot: the fix must not make menus permanently visible, which would be a different falsehood.
